title_lines: TWO HANDS, ONE TOTEM 🤝 His hand walks east–west: that is ∂f/∂x.
Her hand walks north–south: that is ∂f/∂y. On this old dyke,
one of those hands has fallen asleep… 😴 Which sound is this land? 🎧
question: In which sound does the NORTH–SOUTH hand sleep — ∂f/∂y = 0? 😴
hint_lines: Frozen unison lines reveal the sleeping direction. 💡
If north–south sleeps, every north–south row of friends holds ONE note
while east–west staircases up and down. Try each hand on this dyke!

options.label: A
options.explain: BOTH hands were asleep there — one note everywhere, flat land. Here, one hand still changes the music. 🙂

options.label: B
options.explain: Mirror image! There the EAST–WEST hand slept: ∂f/∂x = 0. The frozen rows ran east–west, not north–south. So close — flip it! 🙂

options.label: C
options.explain: Both hands mattered there — the frozen lines ran diagonally, so his steps AND her steps both change the pitch. 🙂

success_text: YES! Every north–south row froze on one note — her steps changed nothing: ∂f/∂y = 0. And option B hid the mirror, ∂f/∂x = 0. A partial derivative is exactly this: one hand at a time. 🎉🤝
